opportunities.title: Young Women in Mind 2026-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity (for at least three years) already delivering therapeutic mental health services; must operate in Northern Ireland, Scotland or the English regions North East, North West, Yorkshire and Humber, the Midlands (or UK-wide/England-wide); either a mental health charity with annual income £750,000+ or a specialist charity led by and for women and girls with annual income £350,000+
opportunities.summary: Collaborative funding programme (with the Prudence Trust and the Julia Rausing Trust) to strengthen and scale gender-specific therapeutic mental health services for girls and young women aged 14-25 across the UK, investing £5 million over three years (2026-2028).

opportunities.title: Preservation and Conservation: Historic buildings and structures

deadlines.raw: Rolling; cut off dates in 2026 are 9 January, 10 April, 31 July, 2 October

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, recognised public body, Community Benefit Society, or Community Interest Company limited by guarantee; project must be UK based, not complete, and focus on a listed building or structure
opportunities.summary: Funding for the preservation and repair of listed historic buildings, structures and architectural features, with special consideration for sustainable conservation and re-use of historic buildings at risk and of outstanding importance. Grants up to £5,000 considered on a rolling basis; larger grants decided quarterly.

opportunities.title: Preservation and Conservation: Conservation of cultural heritage

deadlines.raw: Rolling; cut off dates in 2026 are 9 January, 10 April, 31 July, 2 October

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, recognised public body, Community Benefit Society, or Community Interest Company limited by guarantee; not eligible for AIM and NMCT grant programmes; project must be UK based and not complete
opportunities.summary: Funding for the conservation of culturally and historically significant collections and objects, including works of art, books, significant ephemera, artefacts and archives, carried out by accredited conservators and enabling greater public access.

opportunities.title: Preservation and Conservation: Places of worship

deadlines.raw: Rolling; cut off dates in 2026 are 9 January, 10 April, 31 July, 2 October

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Anglican churches apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme; all other denominations, faiths and cathedrals may apply directly to the Pilgrim Trust
opportunities.summary: Funding for the conservation of historic interiors and historic objects in places of worship open for regular worship, including bells, books, manuscripts, clocks, organs, stained glass, textiles, wall paintings and churchyard structures, and commissioning of conservation reports. Repair grants for buildings open for active worship are no longer provided (redundant/closed places of worship are covered under Historic Buildings and Structures).

opportunities.title: Archives Revealed
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, or recognised public body; project must be UK based and not complete. Apply via the National Archives website.
opportunities.summary: Partnership funding programme (with The National Archives, The National Lottery Heritage Fund and the Wolfson Foundation) dedicated to cataloguing and unlocking archival collections so significant archive collections across the UK are made accessible to the public for research and enjoyment.

opportunities.title: Research, advocacy and development fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Organisations doing research, advocacy and sector development work in young women's mental health and preservation and conservation of historic buildings and collections
opportunities.summary: A fund allowing strategic interventions in the Trust's areas of interest (young women's mental health, and preservation and conservation) where they may bring about systemic change, drive forward policy and practice, or strengthen the sector. Normally partnerships are built and applications invited; the Trust is currently unlikely to support further research/advocacy work in the young women's mental health field.
